challenges.title: A UART receive ring buffer
challenges.prompt: Complete rb_put (store at head, advance, drop and count when full) and rb_get (empty check, read from tail, advance). The buffer holds RB_SIZE-1 bytes so full and empty are distinguishable. A burst of 10 bytes arrives, then the main loop drains it.
challenges.explain: The ISR only writes head and the main loop only writes tail, so a single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer needs no lock; dropping on overflow is safer than overwriting unread data. Verified by compiling and running the solution with gcc.

challenges.title: Debounce and register packing
challenges.prompt: Implement debounce(): the stable state flips only after STABLE_COUNT identical consecutive samples that differ from it, and `*changed` is true only on that sample. The program also packs a mode/enable/channel register; observe the output.
challenges.expected:
sample 6: stable -> PRESSED
sample 12: stable -> RELEASED
reg=0xAD mode=10 en=1 ch=5
challenges.explain: Counting consecutive identical samples filters contact bounce without delay(). Masks and shifts pack fields into a register exactly as peripheral registers are laid out. Verified by compiling and running the solution with gcc.
